tails._explanation: Behind the heads, 12 key 'tails' (7 white-key tail strips + 5 black keys) share one octave. C-E holds 5 tails in 3 white heads; F-B holds 7 tails in 4 heads. With equal heads (W = O/7) the ideal equal tail (O/12) cannot fit both groups: 3W/5 = 14.10 != 4W/7 = 13.43 (quadibloc, datagenetics, mathpages). German practice names two divisions: 'Pianoteilung' (every key equally wide, black keys not all centred) and 'Riegerteilung' (rear/tail keys of F, G and A made wider) - de.wikipedia Klaviatur.

method_equal.description: All 12 tails = O/12 = 13.708 mm; black keys on a uniform 13.708 mm grid (centres at (k+0.5)*O/12). With equal 23.5 mm heads the E|F boundary sits at 70.50 mm at the front but 68.54 mm at the back -> a 1.96 mm jog in E and F (B|C boundary has no jog). Alternative per quadibloc: keep tails equal and make heads unequal: C,D,E heads = 5p/3 = 22.85 mm, F,G,A,B heads = 7p/4 = 23.99 mm (20:21 ratio).

method_group.description: Divide C-E (3 heads = 70.5 mm) into 5 equal tails of 14.10 mm and F-B (4 heads = 94.0 mm) into 7 equal tails of 13.43 mm. Straight E|F and B|C boundaries, G# exactly centred on G|A, D symmetric. Black keys C#/D# are 0.67 mm wider than F#/G#/A# if they fill their tails (datagenetics 'scenario 1': 504 vs 480 units of 5880/octave).

method_identical_sharps.description: mathpages: identical black keys of width B with white tails c=d=e=W-2B/3 and f=g=a=b=W-3B/4; max discrepancy B/12 (used on Roland PC-100). Table uses B = O/12.

giangiulio_measured_organ.description: R. Giangiulio homemade organ manual (Laukhuff-based): octave 164 mm, all sharps 11 mm, naturals 22.15 mm wide at front, 0.050 in (1.27 mm) gap everywhere; white-key tail widths (material, excluding gap): C=D=E 13.97, F=B 12.83, G=A 13.08 mm; sharps 80 mm long, natural fronts 45 mm, overall 126.27 mm. Equivalent to the identical-sharps method with the F-B error split between F/B and G/A.
giangiulio_measured_organ.derived_calc: cumulative (width+1.27) from C left edge; check sum 163.97 vs 164

tails.not_found: No 'Bill Hyde' piano-key-dimension reference could be located.

key_dip_black_derived.calc: sharp sits 1/2 in above naturals at rest and ~1/8 in above naturals when depressed -> 12.7-3.2 = ~9.5 mm

downweight.note: 'about standard'; <45 light, >=55 heavy; Steinway S/M/L taper 50 bass -> 47 treble
>55 g perceived heavy; <=45 g light; note-to-note +/-2 g

upweight.note: for DW 48 g on a new well-lubricated action

measurement_point.note: standard measurement position; DW read from ~4 mm dip

action_leverage.note: measured as hammer rise / 6 mm key dip; worked example 5.4

strike_weight.note: 'Strike weight is the single largest source of inertia in the grand action'

inertia_notes.note: Static touchweight governs soft playing; inertia (strike weight x leverage, key leads) governs force in loud/fast playing. Lead in keys raises key inertia; springs/magnets can lower static touchweight without adding inertia.
Reflected hammer mass at key front ~ SW x leverage^2 ~ 10 g x 5.5^2 ~ 300 g-equivalent (order of magnitude).
Forum observation: digital actions tend to have higher static touchweight but lower moment of inertia than acoustic actions.

digital_actions.name: Roland Hybrid Grand (LX)
digital_actions.confidence: medium (scaled from maker images by forum user)

digital_actions.name: Kawai Grand Feel III / II
digital_actions.hammer_arrangement: Wooden key on balance pins (seesaw) with pivot mid-key; key pushes the weighted hammer upward from the back of the key like a grand; graded key counterweights; let-off; triple sensor.

digital_actions.name: Kawai RHIII
digital_actions.hammer_arrangement: Plastic key pivoting at the back of the key (Kawai); separate weighted hammer lever under the key with its own 'hammer pivot point'; let-off; counterweights; triple sensor.

digital_actions.name: Roland PHA-50
digital_actions.hammer_arrangement: hybrid wood/plastic key with stabilizing pin; hammer under rear of key (per profile image); escapement; triple sensor

digital_actions.name: Roland PHA-4 Standard
digital_actions.hammer_arrangement: all-plastic; hammers are metal-weighted and fold under the FRONT of the keys ('inverted' vs other Roland actions); commonly-circulated side profile images are wrong

digital_actions.name: Yamaha GHS (P-45/P-125)
digital_actions.hammer_arrangement: Hollow plastic keys with NO pin: 'a thin flexible bit of plastic that attaches the keys' (a living hinge); separate hammer lever with one pivot midway and a linkage to the key; weight = thin metal rod, 8 grades; two rubber-dome switches per key; hammers stop between two padded bars.

digital_actions.name: Yamaha GHC (P-145/P-225)
digital_actions.note: GHS successor with shortened pivot length to reduce hidden key length; two sensors; no escapement; downweight rises toward back of key.

digital_actions.name: Yamaha GH3
digital_actions.note: third sensor for repetition; no pivot figure found

digital_actions.name: Casio AP-470 / PX-800
digital_actions.note: 18 cm to pivot with 15 cm visible key (measured)

digital_actions.name: Generic digital hammer action
digital_actions.note: cam under the key presses one end of a hammer, lifting the hammer weight; retaining hook with cushion limits key rise; sensors; pivots.

digital_actions.name: Forum rule of thumb
digital_actions.note: 'once you get much over 20 cm you have quickly diminishing returns'; 24-25 cm felt like the inflection point

floor_to_white_key_top.note: Yamaha grands ~730 mm (28-47/64 in); value read from search-result text of the JS-rendered FAQ
Yamaha factory spec 730-750 mm (uprights vary by model)
measured instruments vary; 'there is no standard'

diy_projects.name: Dovetail (Brian Yu) - 'I 3D Printed a Working Piano'
diy_projects.pivot: compliant mechanisms (printed flexures) instead of pins; modular key units; IR sensors, daisy-chained PCBs
diy_projects.dims: not published in text sources (video only)
diy_projects.lessons: Designer's stated next steps: switch IR -> hall-effect sensors, improve action, different filament; commenters/designer note clicking noise (no felt damping) and durability concerns of plastic flexures.

diy_projects.name: Mechanistic - 3D Printed Grand Piano (24 keys)
diy_projects.pivot: pinned joints ('except for screws, pins, and felt sheets'), accurate grand action geometry
diy_projects.dims: 24 keys; parts split to fit 180x180 mm bed; ~3 kg PLA+, 240 h printing
diy_projects.lessons: Rods used instead of strings because printed plastic creeps under continuous tension (tuning drift, failure over time) - creep is the governing risk for any preloaded printed part.

diy_projects.name: Toast - 3D printable mini piano
diy_projects.pivot: printed keys driving hinged hammers; rubber bands return hammers
diy_projects.dims: mini keyboard; tubes instead of strings
diy_projects.lessons: Iterated hammer-to-key attachment; simplified action because tubes tolerate hammer blocking.

diy_projects.name: PianoClack 'Heathen' - printed action plan
diy_projects.pivot: conventional pinned action planned in PAHT-CF
diy_projects.dims: 5-6 kg filament; hall sensors on keys 16-bit @ ~2 kHz, optical on hammers 100-140 kHz
diy_projects.lessons: PLA creeps; tolerances are stringent and reaming printed holes is hard - PTFE bushings suggested; another builder spent close to $1000 getting printed-part tolerances right; ASA rejected for impact.

diy_projects.name: PianoClack DIY Hickman action
diy_projects.pivot: pin joints: felt-bushed (grand style), inverse-felt, and hard PTFE-tube bushings; 1.5 mm pins in PTFE tube 1.5 ID/3 OD (1.3 mm also used); original Hickman centerpins 1.2-1.4 mm
diy_projects.dims: Janko 5.1 in octave; springs 0.032/0.039/0.047 in piano wire; key weight adjustable ~40-80 g via single lever
diy_projects.lessons: PETG used for 'bendable links'; repetition required adding a driving-lever spring.

diy_projects.name: PianoClack laser-cut action prototype
diy_projects.pivot: no pins: keysticks rest in laser-cut 'combs' with felt glued in the gaps - the keysticks become the pins
diy_projects.dims: 3 mm acrylic keysticks (4.5 mm tried earlier); octave 141 mm then 120 mm prototypes
diy_projects.lessons: Permanently attached weights, no escapement ('constant up-weight'); cutting assembly time was the driver.

diy_projects.name: Cybrid (real AvantGrand N1X action -> MIDI)
diy_projects.dims: 88 keys, 3 CNY70 optical thresholds per hammer, Teensy, ~2 W

diy_projects.name: Arduino forum hall-effect MIDI keyboard
diy_projects.pivot: abandoned piano keys for Wooting Lekker switches
diy_projects.dims: 57 x 49E linear hall sensors in 6x10 matrix
diy_projects.lessons: Per-sensor calibration needed (tolerances); non-linear field vs distance; MCU timing concerns for many keys.

diy_projects.name: Yamaha GHS (commercial reference for a flexure key hinge)
diy_projects.pivot: injection-moulded living hinge: 'The keys ... don't have a hinge or pivot. There's a thin flexible bit of plastic that attaches the keys'
diy_projects.lessons: Reviewer judged it not robust to abuse; see-saw feel ('you can continuously wiggle the keys'). Shows a flexure key pivot is viable in mass production when moulded, not printed.

PETG_prusament.note: printed ISO 527 bars, horizontal; vertical xz: 50 MPa, 1.6 GPa, 5.1 %

fatigue_evidence.note: FDM PLA-wood, fully reversed rotating bending; authors state pure PLA comparable
Derived: FDM PLA endurance ~4-7 MPa at 1e6 cycles => strain amplitude ~0.2-0.3 % (E ~2.3 GPa). ~10 % of yield strain.
PETG FDM tension-tension fatigue (R=0.1) tested at 60-90 % UTS; longitudinal raster best at high stress, diagonal best at 60 % UTS. Full S-N numbers not accessible (paywalled).

low_cycle_static_flexure.note: OpenFlexure PLA flexures t=0.72 mm, l=1.5 mm, w=4 mm, bend <=6 deg; 'close to the yield strain of both PLA and ABS'; no snapping in 6 months, but flexures snapped when over-bent -> use hard stops

hobby_primitive.calc: cantilever eps = 3*t*d/(2*L^2) with t=0.75, L=40, d=5 mm
hobby_primitive.note: Akaki Kuumeri primitive: 0.75 mm thick (2 lines @0.4 nozzle), >=10 mm wide, >=40 mm long, 5 mm tip travel

recommended_for_1e6_to_1e7_cycles.note: engineering judgement: ~10 % of printed yield strain; PLA strongly discouraged (creep, low HDT 55 C)

piano_key_rotation_check.value: 10 mm dip at 200 mm pivot = 0.05 rad (2.9 deg); cross-spring a=0.5 leaf strain = t*theta/(2L) = 0.10 % for t=0.8, L=20 mm

orientation.value: orient so hinge WIDTH is built layer by layer (hinge axis vertical/Z) - bending along extrusion roads, never across layer interfaces
hinge axes horizontal, flexure thickness built from layers (thinner/stronger than min extrusion width)
always print flexure walls vertically; if flat, print lines must run longitudinally; keep seam away from flexure; filleted corners

expected_life.value: FDM living hinges usually for prototypes/few cycles; example: 25 cycles before optimisation; anneal in boiling water and work the hinge

creep.value: 3D printed plastic creeps easily - never leave a flexure under tension; use end stops

centre_shift.value: rho/L = -(sqrt2/30)*(36(a-0.5)^2 - 5); symmetric a=0.5 -> rho/L = 0.236; Haberland a = 0.5 +/- sqrt5/6 (cross at 12.73 % of leaf length) -> rho/L = 0, stiffness 2.67 K_ref; monolithic Haberland rho/L = -0.047, 4 K_ref
